# aqlaboratory/openfoldsparkPowered by Gemini

# aqlaboratory/openfoldsparkPowered by Gemini

Updated onJul 19, 2026Commit[`be2ec18`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/tree/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d)Gemini can make mistakes, so double\-check it\.![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

OpenFold is a PyTorch re\-implementation of AlphaFold 2\. It performs protein structure prediction, generating three\-dimensional protein structures from sequence information for both single proteins and protein complexes\.

 The system's capabilities include:

 - **Protein Structure Prediction:** The AlphaFold2 model architecture iteratively refines protein representations and generates atomic coordinates for both monomers and multimers\. This process is detailed in [AlphaFold2 Model Architecture Implementation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#alphafold2-model-architecture-implementation)\.
- **Data Processing:** Raw biological data is transformed into model\-ready features, leveraging external bioinformatics tools to generate multiple sequence alignments and structural templates\. Refer to [Protein Data Management and Processing](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#protein-data-management-and-processing) for more information\.
- **Geometric Representation:** OpenFold manages protein structures through specialized handling of amino acid properties, 3D geometry, and transformations, including refinement via energy minimization\. See [Protein Structure Representation and Manipulation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#protein-structure-representation-and-manipulation)\.
- **Performance Optimization:** The framework integrates custom CUDA kernels for attention operations and leverages NVIDIA TensorRT for accelerated inference\. Further details are available in [OpenFold Utility Functions and Performance Optimization](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#openfold-utility-functions-and-performance-optimization)\.
- **Database and Environment Management:** A collection of scripts handles database acquisition, alignment generation, environment setup, DeepSpeed configurations, and model checkpoint conversions\. Consult [OpenFold Scripts and Database Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#openfold-scripts-and-database-management)\.
- **Inference and Evaluation:** OpenFold provides tools for running predictions on monomeric proteins and evaluating model performance against native structures\. See [Running OpenFold Inference](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#running-openfold-inference) and [Experimentation and Model Evaluation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#experimentation-and-model-evaluation) for specifics\.## Protein Structure Prediction Core

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

OpenFold is a PyTorch\-based re\-implementation of AlphaFold 2, designed for predicting protein structures\. It incorporates a comprehensive architecture that orchestrates various model components, handles complex numerical operations, and provides a suite of utility functions necessary for protein structure prediction\. The system is engineered to support both monomer and multimer protein predictions\.

 The core of OpenFold's functionality resides in its model architecture, primarily defined within the [`openfold/model`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model) directory\. This architecture is responsible for processing protein sequence and evolutionary information through a series of specialized neural network modules\. The prediction process involves iterative refinement, where previous predictions are fed back into the model to improve accuracy\. For an in\-depth understanding of how these components interact during the prediction process, refer to [Core Model Architecture and Workflow](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#protein-structure-prediction-core-core-model-architecture-and-workflow)\.

 OpenFold integrates external bioinformatics tools to generate essential input data, such as multiple sequence alignments \(MSAs\) and structural templates\. These tools, described further in [External Tool Integration and Data Pipelines](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#protein-structure-prediction-core-external-tool-integration-and-data-pipelines), are crucial for preparing the features that the model uses to infer protein structures\. The [README\.md?plain=1 L48](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/README.md?plain=1#L48) subdirectory within [`openfold`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold) manages the processing of this biological data into a format suitable for the model\.

 Performance optimization is a key aspect of OpenFold, enabling efficient processing of large protein systems and distributed training\. Strategies such as DeepSpeed integration, custom CUDA kernels for attention mechanisms, and TensorRT for inference acceleration are employed to achieve high computational efficiency\. These optimizations are detailed in [Performance Optimization Strategies](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#protein-structure-prediction-core-performance-optimization-strategies)\.

 Utility functions, located in the [`openfold/utils`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils) directory, support various aspects of the prediction pipeline, including structural transformations, feature generation, and the implementation of diverse loss functions used during training\. These functions underpin the model's ability to accurately represent and manipulate protein data, as discussed in [OpenFold Utility Functions and Performance Optimization](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#openfold-utility-functions-and-performance-optimization)\. The system also manages protein data representation and manipulation, including energy minimization and stereochemistry, as outlined in [Protein Structure Representation and Manipulation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#protein-structure-representation-and-manipulation)\.### Core Model Architecture and Workflow

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

OpenFold's core functionality is centered around the [model\.py L66](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/model.py#L66) class, defined in [`openfold/model/model.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/model.py), which orchestrates the entire protein structure prediction workflow\. This class manages the intricate interplay of various components, processing input features, refining protein representations through iterative recycling, and ultimately generating 3D atomic coordinates\.

 The process begins with input embedding, where raw data such as target features, multiple sequence alignment \(MSA\) features, and residue indices are transformed into high\-dimensional representations suitable for the model\. Depending on whether a single protein chain \(monomer\) or multiple interacting chains \(multimer\) are being predicted, an [embedders\.py L158](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/embedders.py#L158), [embedders\.py L313](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/embedders.py#L313), or [embedders\.py L39](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/embedders.py#L39) is used\. Template information, when available, is incorporated into the MSA and pair representations by a [embedders\.py L878](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/embedders.py#L878) or [embedders\.py L635](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/embedders.py#L635)\. Additionally, an [embedders\.py L596](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/embedders.py#L596) and [evoformer\.py L1067](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/evoformer.py#L1067) can process supplementary MSA features to enrich the initial representations\. Details on these embedding modules can be found in [Input Embedding and Recycling Mechanisms](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#alphafold2-model-architecture-implementation-input-embedding-and-recycling-mechanisms)\.

 A distinguishing feature of the AlphaFold model is its iterative recycling mechanism\. Outputs from a previous prediction cycle, including refined MSA, pair, and coordinate embeddings, are fed back into the model to progressively refine the predictions\. This is handled by a [embedders\.py L407](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/embedders.py#L407), which processes these historical embeddings and can even incorporate distogram features derived from previously predicted C\-beta coordinates\. This recycling loop, managed within the [train\_openfold\.py L62](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/train_openfold.py#L62) method of [model\.py L66](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/model.py#L66), can iterate multiple times, with an early stopping criterion based on RMSD differences for multimer predictions\.

 The core of the model's refinement process lies within the Evoformer\. The [model\.py L66](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/model.py#L66) class integrates an [evoformer\.py L769](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/evoformer.py#L769), which is responsible for iteratively processing and refining the MSA and pair representations\. This stack comprises multiple Evoformer blocks that use attention mechanisms and multiplicative updates to capture complex relationships within and between the MSA sequences and residue pairs\. For further details on the Evoformer's building blocks, refer to [Evoformer Blocks and Stacks](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#alphafold2-model-architecture-implementation-evoformer-blocks-and-stacks)\.

 Finally, after the representations are refined by the Evoformer, a [structure\_module\.py L817](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/structure_module.py#L817) converts these abstract representations into concrete 3D atomic coordinates\. This module iteratively builds the protein backbone and side chains, yielding the final predicted protein structure\. The [model\.py L66](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/model.py#L66) model also includes [heads\.py L28](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/heads.py#L28) that compute various auxiliary predictions, such as predicted local distance difference test \(pLDDT\) scores, distograms, and masked MSA predictions, which aid in training and evaluating prediction quality\. The comprehensive loss functions used for training are discussed in [Comprehensive Loss Functions for Structure Prediction](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#openfold-utility-functions-and-performance-optimization-comprehensive-loss-functions-for-structure-prediction)\.

 Throughout this entire process, OpenFold incorporates memory optimization strategies, such as [msa\.py L138](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/msa.py#L138) operations, memory offloading, and activation checkpointing, to manage the computational demands of large protein systems effectively\. These techniques are crucial for enabling the prediction of complex protein structures\. For more on these optimizations, see [Memory Optimization Techniques](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#alphafold2-model-architecture-implementation-memory-optimization-techniques)\.### Evoformer and Attention Mechanisms

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The Evoformer architecture is central to refining protein representations within OpenFold, processing both Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) data and pairwise residue relationships\. Its building blocks include specialized attention mechanisms and multiplicative updates designed to capture complex inter\-residue dependencies\.

 The Evoformer block, primarily implemented in the [evoformer\.py L387](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/evoformer.py#L387) and [evoformer\.py L571](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/evoformer.py#L571) classes within [`openfold/model/evoformer.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/evoformer.py), processes two primary tensor representations: an MSA embedding \([README\.md?plain=1 L33](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/README.md?plain=1#L33)\) and a pair embedding \([vector\.py L28](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/geometry/vector.py#L28)\)\. The [evoformer\.py L769](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/evoformer.py#L769) then orchestrates multiple [evoformer\.py L387](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/evoformer.py#L387) instances, followed by a final linear layer to produce a single embedding from the MSA representation\. Similarly, the [evoformer\.py L1067](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/evoformer.py#L1067) processes additional MSA features\.

 Several attention mechanisms operate within the Evoformer:

 - **MSA Row Attention with Pair Bias:** The [msa\.py L319](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/msa.py#L319) class in [`openfold/model/msa.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/msa.py) applies attention along the rows of the MSA\. It incorporates information from the pair representation \([vector\.py L28](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/geometry/vector.py#L28)\) as a bias to influence attention scores, thereby linking sequence\-level and pairwise structural information\. This is described as Algorithm 7 in AlphaFold2\.
- **MSA Column Attention:** The [msa\.py L348](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/msa.py#L348) class, also in [`openfold/model/msa.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/msa.py), applies attention along the columns of the MSA\. This mechanism allows the model to learn relationships between different residues across all sequences in the alignment \(Algorithm 8\)\. [msa\.py L427](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/msa.py#L427) provides a variant for global column attention\.
- **Triangle Attention:** The [triangular\_attention\.py L32](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/triangular_attention.py#L32) class within [`openfold/model/triangular_attention.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/triangular_attention.py) applies self\-attention to the pair embeddings \([vector\.py L28](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/geometry/vector.py#L28)\) from both starting and ending node perspectives \(Algorithms 13 and 14\)\. This operation enhances the pairwise representation by considering triangular relationships among residues, crucial for refining inter\-residue distances and orientations\.

 In addition to attention, multiplicative updates further refine the pair representation:

 - **Triangle Multiplicative Update:** The [triangular\_multiplicative\_update\.py L177](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/triangular_multiplicative_update.py#L177) class in [`openfold/model/triangular_multiplicative_update.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/triangular_multiplicative_update.py) implements multiplicative updates \(Algorithms 11 and 12\)\. These operations, often referred to as "outgoing" and "incoming," allow information to flow across the 2D pair representation in a manner that reflects underlying structural constraints\. For example, if residues A and B are close, and B and C are close, this update helps reinforce the likelihood of A and C being structurally related\. The implementation also includes [triangular\_multiplicative\_update\.py L736](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/triangular_multiplicative_update.py#L736) and [triangular\_multiplicative\_update\.py L743](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/triangular_multiplicative_update.py#L743) for potential performance gains\.

 The [outer\_product\_mean\.py L27](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/outer_product_mean.py#L27) module in [`openfold/model/outer_product_mean.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/outer_product_mean.py) also plays a role in connecting MSA and pair representations\. It computes an outer product of linearly transformed MSA embeddings to generate an update for the pair embedding \(Algorithm 10\)\. This mechanism allows the model to summarize MSA information into a pairwise context\. The [pair\_transition\.py L24](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/pair_transition.py#L24) module in [`openfold/model/pair_transition.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/pair_transition.py) further processes pair embeddings through a feed\-forward network \(Algorithm 15\)\.

 These components collectively refine the MSA and pair representations, allowing the model to integrate sequence, evolutionary, and structural information to progressively build an accurate 3D model of a protein\. Memory optimization strategies such as chunking, activation checkpointing, and [msa\.py L138](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/msa.py#L138) operations are extensively used across these modules to manage computational resources, particularly for large protein systems\. For further details on how these modules are orchestrated within the overall model, refer to [Core Model Architecture and Workflow](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#protein-structure-prediction-core-core-model-architecture-and-workflow)\.### Auxiliary Heads and Loss Functions

| Head Name | Primary Class | File Location | Function and Predicted Information |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PerResidueLDDTCaPredictor | PerResidueLDDTCaPredictor | openfold/model/heads\.py | Predicts per\-residue confidence scores \(pLDDT\) for the predicted protein structure\. |
| DistogramHead | DistogramHead | openfold/model/heads\.py | Computes a probability distribution of residue\-residue distances \(distogram\)\. |
| MaskedMSAHead | MaskedMSAHead | openfold/model/heads\.py | Reconstructs masked positions in the MSA, used for masked MSA loss\. |
| ExperimentallyResolvedHead | ExperimentallyResolvedHead | openfold/model/heads\.py | Predicts whether each residue is experimentally resolved\. |
| TMScoreHead | TMScoreHead | openfold/model/heads\.py | Predicts pairwise residue scores used in TM\-score, pTM, and ipTM calculations\. |

OpenFold employs various auxiliary prediction heads and corresponding loss functions to train and evaluate protein structure models\. These components allow the model to make predictions beyond the final 3D coordinates, providing additional insights into prediction quality and guiding the training process\. The central orchestrator for these heads is the [heads\.py L28](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/heads.py#L28) class found in [`openfold/model/heads.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/heads.py)\.

 The different auxiliary prediction heads include:

 - **pLDDT \(predicted Local Distance Difference Test\) Predictor**: The [heads\.py L100](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/heads.py#L100) in [`openfold/model/heads.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/heads.py) predicts per\-residue lDDT\-Ca scores\. These scores serve as a per\-residue confidence metric for the predicted local structure, indicating how closely the predicted local environment of a C\-alpha atom matches its true environment\. The output is a set of logits over predefined bins\. The [loss\.py L414](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L414) function from [`openfold/utils/loss.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py) converts these logits into pLDDT scores\.
- **Distogram Predictor**: The [heads\.py L127](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/heads.py#L127) in [`openfold/model/heads.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/heads.py) predicts the probability distribution of inter\-residue distances\. This distogram represents the likelihood of residue pairs being within specific distance bins, offering a coarse\-grained structural prediction that helps guide the model towards accurate 3D arrangements\. This head takes a pairwise embedding as input and outputs logits for various distance bins\. For numerical stability during mixed\-precision training, its internal forward pass for computing probabilities is executed in full precision\.
- **Masked MSA Predictor**: The [heads\.py L203](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/heads.py#L203) in [`openfold/model/heads.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/heads.py) performs a masked multiple sequence alignment \(MSA\) prediction task\. During training, parts of the input MSA are masked, and the model attempts to reconstruct the original amino acids\. This task encourages the model to learn rich representations of sequence co\-evolution and evolutionary relationships within the MSA\.
- **TM\-score Predictor**: The [heads\.py L170](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/heads.py#L170) in [`openfold/model/heads.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/heads.py) predicts information related to the TM\-score, a metric for assessing the topological similarity of two protein structures\. This head helps the model to directly optimize for structural similarity, and its predictions can include overall TM\-score, predicted aligned error \(PAE\), and multimer\-specific scores like predicted interface TM\-score \(pTM\) or weighted predicted TM\-score \(pTM\) based on chain identifiers\. The [loss\.py L670](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L670) and [loss\.py L630](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L630) functions within [`openfold/model/heads.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/heads.py) assist in these calculations\.
- **Experimentally Resolved Predictor**: The [heads\.py L236](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/heads.py#L236) in [`openfold/model/heads.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/heads.py) predicts whether each residue in the input sequence is experimentally resolved\. This can be useful for identifying regions of a protein that are inherently disordered or flexible and thus less likely to be observed in experimental structures\.

 These prediction heads generate various logits and scores, which are then used in corresponding loss functions during model training\. The integration of these auxiliary tasks contributes to the overall stability and accuracy of the protein structure prediction model by providing multiple objectives that guide the learning process towards a comprehensive understanding of protein structure\. A detailed description of the various loss functions used can be found in [Comprehensive Loss Functions for Structure Prediction](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#openfold-utility-functions-and-performance-optimization-comprehensive-loss-functions-for-structure-prediction)\.### External Tool Integration and Data Pipelines

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

OpenFold integrates several external bioinformatics tools to generate multiple sequence alignments \(MSAs\) and template information, which are essential inputs for protein structure prediction\. The data pipelines then process the outputs from these tools, transforming them into a format suitable for the model, supporting both monomer and multimer predictions\.

 The integration of external tools is managed through Python wrappers located primarily in [`openfold/data/tools`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools)\. These wrappers provide an interface to execute binaries such as [index\.md?plain=1 L51](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/index.md?plain=1#L51) for generating MSAs, and [hhsearch\.py L27](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hhsearch.py#L27) and [hmmsearch\.py L27](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hmmsearch.py#L27) for identifying structural templates\. For example, the [hhblits\.py L30](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hhblits.py#L30) class in [`openfold/data/tools/hhblits.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hhblits.py) manages the execution of the [index\.md?plain=1 L51](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/index.md?plain=1#L51) binary against specified protein sequence databases, handling configuration parameters and parsing the resulting A3M format output\. Similarly, the [hhsearch\.py L27](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hhsearch.py#L27) class in [`openfold/data/tools/hhsearch.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hhsearch.py) wraps the [hhsearch\.py L27](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hhsearch.py#L27) binary, processing HMM profiles to find homologous structures and parsing the HHR output\. [jackhmmer\.py L30](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py#L30), wrapped by [`openfold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py), performs iterative sequence database searches\.

 Once these tools generate raw alignment and template data, the data pipelines, largely defined within [`openfold/data/data_pipeline.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_pipeline.py), orchestrate their conversion into model\-ready features\. For monomer predictions, the [data\_pipeline\.py L706](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_pipeline.py#L706) class handles the assembly of sequence features, parsed MSA data, and template hits into a unified feature dictionary\. In the case of multimer predictions, [data\_pipeline\.py L1154](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_pipeline.py#L1154) extends this process by managing MSA pairing and merging across multiple protein chains\. This involves converting monomer features, adding assembly\-specific features like [config\.py L815](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/config.py#L815), [config\.py L843](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/config.py#L843), and [config\.py L824](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/config.py#L824) \(to distinguish chains\), and then performing complex MSA pairing and merging logic, often leveraging functions from [`openfold/data/msa_pairing.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/msa_pairing.py)\.

 The output from the external tools and the subsequent processing steps are then subjected to various data transformations, as detailed in [Protein Data Management and Processing](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#protein-data-management-and-processing), to create the final input tensors for the OpenFold model\.### Performance Optimization Strategies

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

OpenFold employs several strategies to enhance performance and manage memory efficiently, crucial for handling large protein systems and complex models like AlphaFold2\. These include leveraging custom CUDA kernels for core operations, integrating NVIDIA's TensorRT for accelerated inference, and implementing advanced memory management techniques such as chunking and activation checkpointing\.

 Custom CUDA kernels play a significant role in optimizing computationally intensive operations\. For instance, the attention mechanisms, which are central to the Evoformer, utilize custom CUDA kernels for in\-place softmax operations during both forward and backward passes\. This optimization, detailed in [`openfold/utils/kernel/csrc/softmax_cuda_kernel.cu`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/kernel/csrc/softmax_cuda_kernel.cu), improves speed and reduces memory overhead by modifying tensors directly rather than creating new ones\. The [attention\_core\.py L26](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/kernel/attention_core.py#L26) in [`openfold/utils/kernel/attention_core.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/kernel/attention_core.py) wraps these kernels, providing a specialized PyTorch autograd [parsers\.py L274](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/parsers.py#L274) for efficient attention computations\.

 For accelerating inference, OpenFold integrates with NVIDIA TensorRT\. The [tensorrt\_lazy\_compiler\.py L382](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/tensorrt_lazy_compiler.py#L382) in [`openfold/utils/tensorrt_lazy_compiler.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/tensorrt_lazy_compiler.py) enables lazy compilation of PyTorch models or submodules into optimized TensorRT engines\. These engines are serialized and persisted, allowing for faster subsequent inferences\. The integration supports dynamic input shapes, various precision settings \(FP32, TF32, FP16, BF16\), and optional fallback to the original PyTorch model\. The utility function [tensorrt\_utils\.py L27](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/tensorrt_utils.py#L27) in [`openfold/utils/tensorrt_utils.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/tensorrt_utils.py) specifically configures and instruments the model's [config\.py L1010](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/config.py#L1010) component for TensorRT compilation, defining dynamic input shapes and profiles for optimization\.

 Memory management is another key area of optimization\. OpenFold implements chunking, a technique that breaks down large tensors into smaller, manageable chunks for processing\. This is particularly useful in [evoformer\.py L126](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/evoformer.py#L126) and [evoformer\.py L51](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/evoformer.py#L51) within the Evoformer architecture, where [chunk\_utils\.py L213](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/chunk_utils.py#L213) from [`openfold/utils/chunk_utils.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/chunk_utils.py) is used to apply neural network layers chunk by chunk, mitigating memory usage\. The [chunk\_utils\.py L345](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/chunk_utils.py#L345) in [`openfold/utils/chunk_utils.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/chunk_utils.py) dynamically determines optimal chunk sizes to balance performance and memory\.

 Activation checkpointing is also extensively used, especially within the Evoformer blocks and stacks, as seen in [`openfold/model/evoformer.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/evoformer.py)\. This technique reduces memory consumption during training by discarding intermediate activations and recomputing them during the backward pass\. Furthermore, the [model\.py L66](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/model.py#L66) model in [`openfold/model/model.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/model.py) orchestrates these strategies, including memory offloading to move tensors between CPU and GPU during inference, and supports DeepSpeed integration for distributed training and mixed\-precision operations\. The [primitives\.py L138](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/primitives.py#L138) and [primitives\.py L229](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/primitives.py#L229) primitives in [`openfold/model/primitives.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/primitives.py) also include specific handling for [build\_deepspeed\_config\.py L275](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/build_deepspeed_config.py#L275) precision to further optimize performance and memory\.## Protein Data Management and Processing

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

OpenFold's data management and processing framework handles the intricate task of preparing diverse protein data for both single\-chain and multimer prediction scenarios\. This involves systematic data loading, extensive preprocessing, and feature transformation pipelines, alongside the integration of external bioinformatics tools\.

 The data pipeline is primarily managed within the [`openfold/data`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data) directory, which centralizes functionality from raw input files to model\-ready PyTorch tensors\. This includes parsing various biological data formats, featurizing sequences and structures, managing templates, and applying a range of transformations, particularly for multimer complexes\.

 A core component is the [data\_pipeline\.py L706](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_pipeline.py#L706) class found in [`openfold/data/data_pipeline.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_pipeline.py), which orchestrates the assembly of input features for single protein sequences\. It processes FASTA, mmCIF, PDB, and ProteinNet [unpack\_proteinnet\.py L8](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/unpack_proteinnet.py#L8) files, combining sequence features, parsed Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) data, and template hits into a unified feature dictionary\. For multimer complexes, the [data\_pipeline\.py L1154](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_pipeline.py#L1154) extends this functionality, handling the complex tasks of MSA pairing and merging, crucial for accurately representing inter\-chain interactions\.

 External bioinformatics tools are integrated through wrappers located in [`openfold/data/tools`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools)\. These wrappers provide Python interfaces for tools such as [index\.md?plain=1 L51](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/index.md?plain=1#L51), [original\_readme\.md?plain=1 L390](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/original_readme.md?plain=1#L390), [jackhmmer\.py L30](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py#L30), and [kalign\.py L36](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/kalign.py#L36), enabling the execution of sequence search and alignment tasks\. For instance, the [hhblits\.py L30](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hhblits.py#L30) class in [`openfold/data/tools/hhblits.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hhblits.py) facilitates running the [index\.md?plain=1 L51](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/index.md?plain=1#L51) tool for querying FASTA files against protein sequence databases and parsing the A3M output\. Similarly, [hhsearch\.py L27](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hhsearch.py#L27) in [`openfold/data/tools/hhsearch.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hhsearch.py) wraps the [hhsearch\.py L27](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hhsearch.py#L27) binary for HMM profile searches\. These tools are fundamental for generating the MSA and template information required by the OpenFold model\.

 The transformation of raw data into model\-ready features is handled by a rich collection of PyTorch\-based transformation functions defined in [`openfold/data/data_transforms.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_transforms.py) and [`openfold/data/data_transforms_multimer.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_transforms_multimer.py)\. These transformations include operations such as [data\_transforms\.py L164](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_transforms.py#L164) for simulating masking during pretraining, [data\_transforms\.py L186](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_transforms.py#L186) for managing MSA sequence counts, and [data\_transforms\.py L692](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_transforms.py#L692) for generating atom\-level coordinates\. For multimer data, specialized transformations like [data\_transforms\.py L452](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_transforms.py#L452) and [data\_transforms\.py L1183](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_transforms.py#L1183) in [`openfold/data/data_transforms_multimer.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_transforms_multimer.py) address the unique challenges of processing protein complexes, including strategies to preserve inter\-chain interactions during cropping\.

 The parsing of mmCIF files is managed by [`openfold/data/mmcif_parsing.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/mmcif_parsing.py), which converts complex mmCIF data into structured Python objects \([mmcif\_parsing\.py L79](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/mmcif_parsing.py#L79)\) containing Biopython structures, sequence information, and mappings between sequence residues and structural positions\. This structured representation facilitates downstream processing and feature extraction\.

 Overall, the data management and processing aspects of OpenFold ensure that the model receives consistently formatted, augmented, and rich feature sets, critical for accurate protein structure prediction\.### Data Loading and Processing Pipelines

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

OpenFold's data loading and processing pipelines facilitate the preparation of protein sequence and structural data for both single\-chain \(monomer\) and multimeric prediction tasks\. These pipelines orchestrate the conversion of raw biological inputs into a structured format that the model can consume\.

 The core data loading mechanisms are implemented in [`openfold/data/data_modules.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_modules.py)\. This file defines dataset classes, such as [data\_modules\.py L26](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_modules.py#L26) for single protein chains and [data\_modules\.py L292](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_modules.py#L292) for multimeric complexes\. These datasets manage the ingestion of various protein data formats, including mmCIF, PDB, and FASTA files, alongside associated alignment and template data\. They also integrate with caching mechanisms to optimize data access\. For training, [data\_modules\.py L535](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_modules.py#L535) and [data\_modules\.py L664](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_modules.py#L664) apply stochastic and deterministic filtering strategies, crucial for selecting diverse and high\-quality data during model training, mirroring practices in AlphaFold\. Data loaders, such as [data\_modules\.py L762](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_modules.py#L762), extend standard PyTorch functionality to dynamically inject batch properties, like the number of recycling iterations, which can influence model behavior per batch\.

 The [data\_pipeline\.py L706](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_pipeline.py#L706) classes in [`openfold/data/data_pipeline.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_pipeline.py) are central to orchestrating the assembly of input features\. [data\_pipeline\.py L706](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_pipeline.py#L706) handles monomer scenarios, generating sequence, MSA, and template features from raw inputs\. [data\_pipeline\.py L1154](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_pipeline.py#L1154) extends this for multimeric proteins, performing critical steps such as MSA pairing and merging across multiple chains, which is essential for modeling inter\-chain interactions\. These pipelines also manage the execution of external bioinformatics tools for alignment generation\. Further details on these external tools can be found in [External Bioinformatics Tool Integration](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#protein-data-management-and-processing-external-bioinformatics-tool-integration)\.

 Raw features, once processed by the data pipelines, are further transformed into PyTorch tensors suitable for model input by the [feature\_pipeline\.py L132](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/feature_pipeline.py#L132) in [`openfold/data/feature_pipeline.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/feature_pipeline.py)\. This component applies configuration\-driven preprocessing and feature selection, ensuring that data is correctly typed and formatted\. Finally, the transformation functions defined in [`openfold/data/input_pipeline.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/input_pipeline.py) and [`openfold/data/input_pipeline_multimer.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/input_pipeline_multimer.py) are applied\. These orchestrate sequential data transformations, including those applied once per input and those ensembled across recycling iterations to refine predictions\. These transformations involve tasks such as feature casting, MSA processing, template processing, and data cropping to manage input sizes\. The specific transformations applied are detailed further in [Feature Transformation and Augmentation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#protein-data-management-and-processing-feature-transformation-and-augmentation)\.### Multimer\-Specific Data Handling

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

OpenFold addresses the complexities of predicting structures for protein multimers by implementing specialized data handling strategies that extend beyond those used for single protein chains\. This involves intricate Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) pairing, feature merging, and multimer\-specific transformations and cropping\.

 The process of preparing multimer data begins with the processing of individual protein chains, which is then followed by the critical step of MSA pairing\. MSA pairing is the process of aligning sequences from different protein chains within a multimer, considering both shared evolutionary history and potential inter\-chain interactions\. This is managed by the functions within [`openfold/data/msa_pairing.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/msa_pairing.py), which reorder and pair MSA features \([msa\_pairing\.py L80](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/msa_pairing.py#L80) variants\) based on sequence similarity\. A key aspect is the [msa\_pairing\.py L56](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/msa_pairing.py#L56) function, which orchestrates the pairing of MSA sequences across all provided chains, using [msa\_pairing\.py L145](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/msa_pairing.py#L145) to identify and sort paired rows\. This module also handles homomers \(identical chains\) by merging their features\. Once MSAs are paired, redundant unpaired sequences are removed using [msa\_pairing\.py L462](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/msa_pairing.py#L462) to streamline the feature set\.

 Following MSA pairing, the system integrates these individual chain features into a unified representation suitable for multimer modeling\. The [msa\_pairing\.py L432](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/msa_pairing.py#L432) function within [`openfold/data/msa_pairing.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/msa_pairing.py) plays a central role here, intelligently concatenating or block\-diagonalizing features based on their type and whether MSA sequences have been paired\. This ensures that all relevant data, including sequence, MSA, and template information, is correctly assembled for the multimer\.

 Multimer\-specific transformations and cropping strategies are then applied to manage memory and computational load while preserving crucial interaction information\. The [data\_transforms\.py L1183](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_transforms.py#L1183) function, defined in [`openfold/data/data_transforms_multimer.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_transforms_multimer.py), is essential for handling varying sequence lengths and limiting input sizes\. This function can prioritize cropping around interface residues through [data\_transforms\_multimer\.py L336](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_transforms_multimer.py#L336) to maintain inter\-chain contacts or select contiguous blocks from chains using [data\_transforms\_multimer\.py L376](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_transforms_multimer.py#L376)\. It also subsamples templates if necessary\. The transformations also include sophisticated methods for generating masked MSAs and clustering techniques to summarize extra MSA sequences, providing richer input to the model\. These transformations are orchestrated by [input\_pipeline\.py L70](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/input_pipeline.py#L70) in [`openfold/data/input_pipeline_multimer.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/input_pipeline_multimer.py), which are applied multiple times during the iterative recycling process to refine predictions\.

 Ultimately, this comprehensive approach to multimer data processing ensures that OpenFold can effectively model protein complexes by providing a robust and structured representation of their sequence, evolutionary, and structural information\. More details on the broader data processing architecture are available in [Protein Data Management and Processing](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#protein-data-management-and-processing)\.### External Bioinformatics Tool Integration

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

OpenFold integrates several external bioinformatics tools to generate Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\) and extract template information, which are crucial for protein structure prediction\. These tools are wrapped in Python classes within the [`openfold/data/tools`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools) directory, abstracting their command\-line execution and output parsing\.

 For protein sequence searches and MSA generation, OpenFold utilizes [index\.md?plain=1 L51](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/index.md?plain=1#L51) and [jackhmmer\.py L30](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py#L30)\. [index\.md?plain=1 L51](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/index.md?plain=1#L51) \([`openfold/data/tools/hhblits.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hhblits.py)\) is employed to query protein sequence databases and produce A3M\-formatted MSAs\. Similarly, [jackhmmer\.py L30](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py#L30) \([`openfold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py)\) performs iterative sequence database searches\. Both wrappers handle the execution of these binaries, manage temporary files for input and output, and provide mechanisms to configure search parameters like E\-value thresholds and the number of iterations\. For large databases, the [jackhmmer\.py L30](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py#L30) wrapper supports a streaming mechanism, processing database chunks concurrently to optimize performance\.

 Once MSAs are generated or when an existing MSA is available, Hidden Markov Model \(HMM\) profiles can be built using [hmmbuild\.py L25](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hmmbuild.py#L25) \([`openfold/data/tools/hmmbuild.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hmmbuild.py)\)\. This tool converts A3M or Stockholm\-formatted MSAs into HMM profiles, which can then be used for more sensitive database searches\.

 For template identification, OpenFold employs [original\_readme\.md?plain=1 L390](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/original_readme.md?plain=1#L390) \([`openfold/data/tools/hhsearch.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hhsearch.py)\) and [hmmsearch\.py L27](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hmmsearch.py#L27) \([`openfold/data/tools/hmmsearch.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hmmsearch.py)\)\. [original\_readme\.md?plain=1 L390](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/original_readme.md?plain=1#L390) queries protein sequence databases using HMM profiles and outputs HHR files, which contain detailed alignment information\. The [hmmsearch\.py L27](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hmmsearch.py#L27) tool operates similarly, searching a profile against a sequence database, with its output often in Stockholm format\. The [hhsearch\.py L27](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hhsearch.py#L27) wrapper parses the HHR output into structured [parsers\.py L57](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/parsers.py#L57) objects\. The [hmmsearch\.py L27](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hmmsearch.py#L27) wrapper, on the other hand, converts its Stockholm output to A3M format and then parses it into [parsers\.py L57](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/parsers.py#L57) objects\. These [parsers\.py L57](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/parsers.py#L57) objects capture essential details of detected homologous structures, such as alignment scores, hit sequences, and residue indices\.

 Finally, for generating multiple sequence alignments directly from a set of sequences, the [kalign\.py L36](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/kalign.py#L36) tool \([`openfold/data/tools/kalign.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/kalign.py)\) is integrated\. Its wrapper takes a sequence of protein strings and returns the alignment in A3M format\.

 The parsing of outputs from these various tools is centralized in [`openfold/data/parsers.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/parsers.py)\. This module defines classes like [parsers\.py L29](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/parsers.py#L29) and [parsers\.py L57](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/parsers.py#L57) to represent parsed data consistently\. It includes functions to parse FASTA, Stockholm, A3M, HHR, and TBLOUT formats, ensuring that the raw outputs from the external tools are converted into a format readily usable by the OpenFold model for feature generation\. The file [`openfold/data/tools/parse_msa_files.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/parse_msa_files.py) further orchestrates the parallel parsing of multiple MSA files from a directory, serializing the results for efficient data handling\. Utility functions for temporary directory management and timing \([`openfold/data/tools/utils.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/utils.py)\) support the execution of these external tools, ensuring clean and efficient operations\.### Feature Transformation and Augmentation

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

OpenFold employs a comprehensive set of PyTorch\-based data transformations and augmentations to prepare raw protein data for its prediction models\. These operations are crucial for converting diverse biological information into a standardized, model\-ready format, and for enhancing model robustness through various augmentation techniques\.

 The transformations are organized into pipelines, often driven by configuration settings that adapt behavior based on the processing mode \(e\.g\., training, evaluation, prediction\) and the type of protein \(monomer or multimer\)\. The core logic for these transformations is primarily housed in [`openfold/data/data_transforms.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_transforms.py), while their orchestration into input pipelines for monomers and multimers is managed by [`openfold/data/input_pipeline.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/input_pipeline.py) and [`openfold/data/input_pipeline_multimer.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/input_pipeline_multimer.py), respectively\. The [feature\_pipeline\.py L132](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/feature_pipeline.py#L132) in [`openfold/data/feature_pipeline.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/feature_pipeline.py) acts as a central orchestrator, converting raw NumPy\-based features into PyTorch tensors and applying these configuration\-driven preprocessing steps\.

 Key transformations include standardizing amino acid types, handling sequence and multiple sequence alignment \(MSA\) masks, and generating pseudo\-beta carbon positions for simplified structural representations\. A notable augmentation strategy involves [data\_transforms\.py L164](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_transforms.py#L164), which simulates masking of MSA entries, a technique commonly used in pretraining models to improve generalization\. Similarly, [data\_transforms\.py L452](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_transforms.py#L452) implements a more detailed masking strategy where residues are randomly replaced to simulate uncertainty or partial information\.

 For managing computational resources and optimizing model performance, several transformations focus on adjusting input dimensions\. Functions like [data\_transforms\.py L186](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_transforms.py#L186) allow for the selection of a subset of MSA sequences, with unselected sequences optionally stored as [config\.py L241](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/config.py#L241)\. The [data\_transforms\.py L505](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_transforms.py#L505) function is crucial for deep learning models, as it pads or truncates various features to predefined fixed dimensions, enabling efficient batch processing\. Data augmentation also includes [data\_transforms\.py L1183](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_transforms.py#L1183), which randomly crops the residue dimension of relevant features, thereby enhancing the model's ability to generalize across different protein lengths\.

 Beyond sequence and MSA processing, OpenFold also generates essential geometric features\. This includes converting atom37 coordinates into [rigid\_utils\.py L813](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/rigid_utils.py#L813) transformations \(frames\) for the protein backbone and side chains, and deriving torsion angles \(e\.g\., phi, psi, chi angles\) from atomic coordinates\. These geometric representations provide the model with a rich understanding of the protein's 3D structure\. The system also supports the integration of template information, transforming template amino acid types and generating pseudo\-beta coordinates for templates, which can significantly aid prediction accuracy\.

 The design emphasizes the use of PyTorch for all tensor operations, ensuring compatibility with the model's architecture\. The extensive use of masks \(e\.g\., [config\.py L367](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/config.py#L367), [train\_openfold\.py L172](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/train_openfold.py#L172), [model\.py L356](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/model.py#L356)\) across these transformations is fundamental for handling missing data, padding, and invalid positions consistently\. This modular and configurable approach to feature transformation and augmentation allows OpenFold to process a wide array of protein data effectively, preparing it for the complex predictions carried out by the AlphaFold2 model [AlphaFold2 Model Architecture Implementation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#alphafold2-model-architecture-implementation)\.### Template Search and Featurization

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The OpenFold framework processes template information, derived from sources like HHsearch and HMMsearch results or custom mmCIF files, to extract structural and sequence features essential for protein structure prediction\. This process involves converting raw template search hits into a structured feature dictionary that describes the template's amino acid sequence, atom positions, and atom masks, all aligned to the query sequence\.

 Key to this process is the prefiltering of template hits, where templates are assessed based on criteria such as release date, alignment ratio, and redundancy with the query sequence\. This prefiltering step, implemented in functions like [templates\.py L220](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/templates.py#L220) within [`openfold/data/templates.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/templates.py), prevents computationally expensive full mmCIF parsing and detailed feature extraction for unsuitable templates\.

 Once a template is deemed suitable, its corresponding mmCIF file is parsed to extract detailed structural information\. The [download\_cameo\.py L9](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_cameo.py#L9) module, primarily the [mmcif\_parsing\.py L178](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/mmcif_parsing.py#L178) function in [`openfold/data/mmcif_parsing.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/mmcif_parsing.py), converts the mmCIF format into structured Python objects \([mmcif\_parsing\.py L79](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/mmcif_parsing.py#L79)\), which encapsulate the Biopython structure, sequence information, and mappings between sequence residues and structural positions\. This module also handles cases where PDB IDs have become obsolete, ensuring that up\-to\-date structural data is used\.

 A crucial step is the realignment of template sequences from search hits with the actual sequences found in the parsed mmCIF files\. This is often necessary because discrepancies can arise between the sequences reported by search tools and the definitive sequences in structural databases\. The [templates\.py L366](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/templates.py#L366) function in [`openfold/data/templates.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/templates.py) employs an external tool, [kalign\.py L36](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/kalign.py#L36), to perform robust sequence alignment when such differences are significant\. Following realignment, atom positions and masks are extracted, with checks to ensure the structural integrity of the template, such as verifying C\-alpha distances between adjacent residues\.

 The extracted features are then consolidated into a [templates\.py L1017](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/templates.py#L1017) by specialized featurizers like [templates\.py L1105](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/templates.py#L1105) and [templates\.py L1225](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/templates.py#L1225) in [`openfold/data/templates.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/templates.py) for standard search tool outputs, or [templates\.py L1208](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/templates.py#L1208) for user\-provided templates\. These featurizers manage the iterative processing of hits, sorting them by confidence scores, and selecting a specified number of the most promising templates for feature generation\.## AlphaFold2 Model Architecture Implementation

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The OpenFold implementation of the AlphaFold2 model architecture for protein structure prediction, found primarily in [`openfold/model`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model), is a comprehensive system designed to accurately predict the three\-dimensional structures of proteins, including multimeric complexes\. This architecture orchestrates various modules to process input features, iteratively refine intermediate representations, and ultimately generate a protein's atomic coordinates\.

 At its core, the model is built around the [model\.py L66](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/model.py#L66) class, defined in [`openfold/model/model.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/model.py)\. This class manages the entire prediction pipeline, from initial data embedding to final structure generation\. It integrates modules for handling diverse input features, including multiple sequence alignments \(MSAs\) and structural templates, and supports both single\-chain \(monomer\) and multi\-chain \(multimer\) protein predictions\. A key feature of this design is the iterative recycling mechanism, where outputs from a previous prediction cycle are fed back into the model as refined inputs, allowing for progressive improvement of the predicted structure\. This iterative refinement helps the model converge on more accurate predictions\. The [model\.py L66](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/model.py#L66) class is also designed with memory optimization in mind, employing strategies such as offloading computations to the CPU and activation checkpointing to manage the substantial memory requirements of large protein systems\.

 The model begins by transforming raw input data into high\-dimensional numerical representations through various embedding modules\. These modules, located in [`openfold/model/embedders.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/embedders.py), convert target features, MSA features, and relative positional information into initial MSA and pair embeddings\. For multimeric proteins, specialized embedders, such as [embedders\.py L158](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/embedders.py#L158), incorporate chain\-aware relative positional encodings, which are essential for understanding inter\-chain relationships\. Recycling embeddings, generated by the [embedders\.py L407](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/embedders.py#L407), process previous iteration outputs to update these initial representations, enhancing the model's ability to refine its predictions over successive cycles\. Template information is also embedded, leveraging structural data from known proteins to guide the prediction process\. For further details on how data is loaded and processed, refer to [Protein Data Management and Processing](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#protein-data-management-and-processing)\.

 The central processing unit of the AlphaFold2 architecture is the Evoformer, implemented through [evoformer\.py L769](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/evoformer.py#L769) and [evoformer\.py L1067](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/evoformer.py#L1067) in [`openfold/model/evoformer.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/evoformer.py)\. These stacks consist of multiple [evoformer\.py L387](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/evoformer.py#L387) and [evoformer\.py L571](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/evoformer.py#L571) instances, which iteratively refine the MSA and pair representations\. The Evoformer blocks utilize specialized attention mechanisms, detailed in [Evoformer and Attention Mechanisms](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#protein-structure-prediction-core-evoformer-and-attention-mechanisms), such as row\-wise and column\-wise MSA attention with pair bias, to capture complex dependencies within and between protein sequences and their pairwise relationships\. Additionally, triangular multiplicative updates, implemented in [`openfold/model/triangular_multiplicative_update.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/triangular_multiplicative_update.py), are applied to the pair representations, further enhancing the model's understanding of inter\-residue relationships\. The [outer\_product\_mean\.py L27](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/outer_product_mean.py#L27) module, defined in [`openfold/model/outer_product_mean.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/outer_product_mean.py), contributes to the refinement of pair representations by integrating information from the MSA\.

 Following the Evoformer, the [structure\_module\.py L817](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/structure_module.py#L817), located in [`openfold/model/structure_module.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/structure_module.py), is responsible for translating the refined MSA and pair representations into 3D atomic coordinates\. This module iteratively builds the protein structure by predicting torsion angles and updating the protein backbone's rigid transformations\. It uses an [structure\_module\.py L209](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/structure_module.py#L209) mechanism to refine the single representation, considering both scalar features and 3D points\. The [structure\_module\.py L817](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/structure_module.py#L817) generates the final set of atomic coordinates, which define the predicted protein structure\. For more on the utilities used for structural manipulation, refer to [Protein Structure Representation and Manipulation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#protein-structure-representation-and-manipulation)\.

 Finally, the model includes [heads\.py L28](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/heads.py#L28), defined in [`openfold/model/heads.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/heads.py), which perform various auxiliary prediction tasks\. These heads predict properties such as predicted local distance difference test \(pLDDT\) scores, distograms \(inter\-residue distance distributions\), and masked MSA tokens\. These predictions serve as crucial targets during training and provide additional quality metrics for the predicted structures\. More details on these can be found in [Auxiliary Heads and Loss Functions](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#protein-structure-prediction-core-auxiliary-heads-and-loss-functions)\. Throughout these modules, foundational components like [primitives\.py L138](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/primitives.py#L138) and [primitives\.py L229](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/primitives.py#L229) with bfloat16 handling, along with various attention implementations optimized for performance, are provided in [`openfold/model/primitives.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/primitives.py)\.### Input Embedding and Recycling Mechanisms

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The protein structure prediction process begins with sophisticated input embedding strategies that transform raw biological data into numerical representations understandable by the model\. This involves several [embedders\.py L39](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/embedders.py#L39) modules found in [`openfold/model/embedders.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/embedders.py), which process diverse data types such as target features, multiple sequence alignments \(MSAs\), and template information\.
