 A core set of utilities focuses on managing different atomic representations, specifically converting between [feats\.py L56](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/feats.py#L56) \(14 common atoms per residue\) and [loss\.py L798](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L798) \(a superset including additional atoms\) using functions like [feats\.py L56](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/feats.py#L56) and [all\_atom\_multimer\.py L58](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/all_atom_multimer.py#L58) in [`openfold/utils/all_atom_multimer.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/all_atom_multimer.py)\. This flexibility allows models to operate at varying levels of atomic detail\.

 Another significant area involves the creation and manipulation of rigid body frames, which define local coordinate systems within a protein\. The [data\_transforms\.py L795](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_transforms.py#L795) function in [`openfold/utils/all_atom_multimer.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/all_atom_multimer.py) computes up to eight rigid body frames per residue, crucial for describing the local orientation of different parts of a residue \(e\.g\., backbone, side chains\)\. Conversely, [feats\.py L185](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/feats.py#L185) \(in [`openfold/utils/all_atom_multimer.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/all_atom_multimer.py) and [`openfold/utils/feats.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/feats.py)\) converts torsion angles \(such as chi angles\) into a hierarchy of these rigid frames\. The [feats\.py L253](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/feats.py#L253) function \(in [`openfold/utils/all_atom_multimer.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/all_atom_multimer.py) and [`openfold/utils/feats.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/feats.py)\) uses these computed frames along with idealized literature positions to reconstruct [feats\.py L56](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/feats.py#L56) coordinates\. These functions are essential for both converting predicted abstract representations into concrete 3D structures and for analyzing existing structures\.

 The calculation of chi torsion angles is directly supported by [all\_atom\_multimer\.py L369](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/all_atom_multimer.py#L369) in [`openfold/utils/all_atom_multimer.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/all_atom_multimer.py)\. This function identifies the specific atoms needed for each chi angle for all standard amino acid types and computes the angles, which are vital for understanding side\-chain conformations\.

 The system also includes basic backbone transformations, such as [all\_atom\_multimer\.py L477](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/all_atom_multimer.py#L477) in [`openfold/utils/all_atom_multimer.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/all_atom_multimer.py), which generates a [rigid\_matrix\_vector\.py L30](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py#L30) \(a 3D rigid transformation object\) for the protein backbone from its N, C\_alpha, and C atoms\. This transformation defines the local coordinate system of the backbone, enabling further structural analyses\. These operations rely on geometric primitives like [rigid\_matrix\_vector\.py L30](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py#L30), [rotation\_matrix\.py L30](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L30), and [vector\.py L25](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/geometry/vector.py#L25) defined in [Advanced 3D Geometric Data Structures and Operations](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#openfold-utility-functions-and-performance-optimization-advanced-3d-geometric-data-structures-and-operations)\.### Advanced 3D Geometric Data Structures and Operations

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

OpenFold implements custom 3D geometric data structures to efficiently represent and manipulate vectors, rotation matrices, and rigid transformations using [msa\.py L93](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/msa.py#L93)s\. These structures are designed for batched operations and integrate with neural networks\.

 The [vector\.py L25](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/geometry/vector.py#L25) dataclass, defined in [`openfold/utils/geometry/vector.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/geometry/vector.py), provides functionality for 3D vectors, supporting arithmetic operations, dot and cross products, and norm calculations\. It is also used in calculating geometric properties such as square Euclidean distance, Euclidean distance, and dihedral angles\.

 For 3x3 rotation matrices, OpenFold uses the [rotation\_matrix\.py L30](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L30) dataclass from [`openfold/utils/geometry/rotation_matrix.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/geometry/rotation_matrix.py)\. This structure supports matrix multiplication, inversion, and the application of rotations to points\. It also handles conversions between rotation matrix and quaternion representations, and can construct rotations from two vectors\.

 The [rigid\_matrix\_vector\.py L30](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py#L30) dataclass, located in [`openfold/utils/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py), combines [rotation\_matrix\.py L30](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L30) for rotation and [vector\.py L25](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/geometry/vector.py#L25) for translation to represent 3D rigid transformations\. It offers operations for composing transformations, inverting them, and applying them to points\. Conversions to and from 4x4 homogeneous matrices are also supported, alongside various batch operations like reshaping and concatenation\.

 For integrating these geometric transformations within neural networks, the [quat\_rigid\.py L10](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/geometry/quat_rigid.py#L10) module in [`openfold/utils/geometry/quat_rigid.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/geometry/quat_rigid.py) converts neural network activations into [rigid\_matrix\_vector\.py L30](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py#L30) transformations\. This module can utilize either full \(4\-component\) or partial \(3\-component with implicit 1\.0 scalar\) quaternion representations for rotations\.

 These data structures, along with the utility functions found in [`openfold/utils/geometry`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/geometry), form the foundation for all 3D structural manipulations within OpenFold, as further detailed in [Protein Structural and Coordinate Transformations](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#openfold-utility-functions-and-performance-optimization-protein-structural-and-coordinate-transformations)\.### Comprehensive Loss Functions for Structure Prediction

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

OpenFold implements a suite of loss functions, primarily found in [`openfold/utils/loss.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py), designed to guide the training of protein structure prediction models by penalizing discrepancies between predictions and ground truth\. The [loss\.py L1685](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L1685) module orchestrates the calculation and aggregation of these individual loss components, applying configurable weights and managing the overall training objective\.

 A central component is the Frame Aligned Point Error \(FAPE\) loss, computed by [loss\.py L82](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L82)\. This loss measures the distance between predicted and ground\-truth atomic positions within the local coordinate frame of predicted rigid bodies, crucial for refining both backbone and side\-chain structures\. Specifically, [loss\.py L169](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L169) and [loss\.py L235](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L235) utilize FAPE for their respective components\.

 Beyond atomic coordinates, OpenFold also evaluates predictions using distance\-based metrics\. [loss\.py L507](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L507) computes a categorical cross\-entropy loss on binned lDDT\-CA scores, assessing the local structural similarity of C\-alpha atoms\. Similarly, [loss\.py L562](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L562) calculates cross\-entropy for predicted residue\-residue distances\. [loss\.py L721](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L721) is responsible for a categorical cross\-entropy loss on binned TM\-score values, which gauges the topological and structural similarity between protein structures\.

 To ensure chemically plausible predictions, OpenFold incorporates [loss\.py L1432](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L1432), which aggregates penalties for various structural anomalies\. These include [loss\.py L782](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L782) \(for peptide bond geometry\), [loss\.py L942](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L942) \(for steric clashes between different residues\), and [loss\.py L1096](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L1096) \(for issues within a single residue\)\. The [loss\.py L1186](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L1186) function identifies and quantifies these issues\.

 The model also includes [loss\.py L1595](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L1595), which is a BERT\-style masked language modeling objective applied to the multiple sequence alignment \(MSA\), helping the model learn sequence\-level representations\. For multimeric proteins, [loss\.py L1628](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L1628) penalizes deviations in the distances between the centers of mass of different chains, promoting accurate quaternary structure predictions\.

 Other specialized losses include [loss\.py L328](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L328) for torsion angles, and [loss\.py L1571](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L1571) for penalizing mispredictions of experimentally unresolved atoms\. To handle the intrinsic symmetries of certain amino acids, [loss\.py L1463](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/loss.py#L1463) dynamically renames symmetric ground\-truth atoms to minimize prediction error, ensuring consistent and fair evaluation\.### Custom CUDA Kernels for Optimized Attention

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

OpenFold accelerates its attention mechanisms through custom CUDA kernels, which are implemented within the [`openfold/utils/kernel`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/kernel) directory\. The primary component for this optimization is the [attention\_core\.py L26](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/kernel/attention_core.py#L26), a [attention\_core\.py L26](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/kernel/attention_core.py#L26)\. This function handles the forward and backward passes for attention operations, particularly by applying custom CUDA kernels for in\-place modifications to attention logits\. This approach allows for efficient computation, especially for large models and datasets\.

 The core CUDA implementation for these optimized operations is found in [`openfold/utils/kernel/csrc/softmax_cuda_kernel.cu`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/kernel/csrc/softmax_cuda_kernel.cu)\. This file contains specialized kernels, such as [softmax\_cuda\_kernel\.cu L49](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/kernel/csrc/softmax_cuda_kernel.cu#L49) for the forward pass and [softmax\_cuda\_kernel\.cu L133](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/kernel/csrc/softmax_cuda_kernel.cu#L133) for the backward pass, which perform in\-place softmax operations\. These kernels leverage warp\-level reductions, a technique that optimizes computations on NVIDIA GPUs by coordinating threads within a warp to reduce global memory access and increase parallelism\. The C\+\+ interface in [`openfold/utils/kernel/csrc/softmax_cuda.cpp`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/kernel/csrc/softmax_cuda.cpp) exposes these CUDA kernels to Python, making them accessible from the PyTorch environment\. Compatibility with different PyTorch versions is maintained through common header files in [`openfold/utils/kernel/csrc/compat.h`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/kernel/csrc/compat.h), ensuring that the optimized kernels function across various development environments\.### Multi\-Chain Permutation Alignment

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Predicting the structure of multi\-chain proteins presents a unique challenge: models may output chains in an arbitrary order, differing from the ground truth\. To address this, OpenFold includes utilities to align predicted protein chains with their corresponding ground truth chains by finding the optimal permutation that minimizes the Root Mean Square Deviation \(RMSD\)\.

 The central function for this process is [multi\_chain\_permutation\.py L515](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/multi_chain_permutation.py#L515) in [`openfold/utils/multi_chain_permutation.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/multi_chain_permutation.py)\. This function orchestrates the alignment, ensuring that model predictions can be correctly compared against experimental structures\. It takes model outputs and ground truth data, returning the ground truth features reordered to match the optimally permuted predicted chains\.

 The alignment process is managed by [multi\_chain\_permutation\.py L430](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/multi_chain_permutation.py#L430), which determines the best chain permutation\. This involves several steps:

 - **Anchor Selection:** To initiate the alignment robustly, an "anchor" chain is selected from the ground truth\. This anchor is typically the chain with the least asymmetry or the longest length, identified by functions such as [multi\_chain\_permutation\.py L111](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/multi_chain_permutation.py#L111)\. This provides a reliable starting point for the transformation process\.
- **Optimal Transformation:** The [multi\_chain\_permutation\.py L35](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/multi_chain_permutation.py#L35) function implements the Kabsch algorithm to find the optimal 3D rotation matrix that aligns two sets of points\. This is complemented by [multi\_chain\_permutation\.py L64](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/multi_chain_permutation.py#L64), which also calculates the optimal translation vector\. These functions are crucial for superimposing predicted atomic coordinates onto ground truth coordinates, minimizing the spatial difference between them\.
- **Greedy Alignment:** Once an anchor is established and transformations can be computed, [multi\_chain\_permutation\.py L167](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/multi_chain_permutation.py#L167) iteratively matches predicted chains to ground truth chains\. It operates by finding the unused ground truth chain that, when aligned with a predicted chain, yields the lowest RMSD\. This greedy approach efficiently builds up the optimal permutation\.
- **RMSD Calculation:** The [multi\_chain\_permutation\.py L10](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/multi_chain_permutation.py#L10) function calculates the Root Mean Square Deviation between two sets of atom positions, serving as the primary metric for evaluating alignment quality during the permutation search\.

 After determining the optimal permutation and transformation, ground truth features are adjusted using functions like [multi\_chain\_permutation\.py L249](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/multi_chain_permutation.py#L249) and [msa\_pairing\.py L91](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/msa_pairing.py#L91)\. These ensure that the ground truth data aligns correctly with the model's output structure, facilitating accurate loss calculation during training or evaluation\. The module heavily leverages [setup\.py L20](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/setup.py#L20) tensors for efficient, GPU\-accelerated numerical operations, crucial for performance in deep learning contexts\.### TensorRT Integration for Inference Acceleration

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

OpenFold integrates with NVIDIA TensorRT to accelerate inference by compiling PyTorch models into optimized TensorRT engines\. This process involves a [tensorrt\_lazy\_compiler\.py L382](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/tensorrt_lazy_compiler.py#L382) that lazily and persistently compiles models, enabling dynamic input shapes and precision control\.

 The [tensorrt\_lazy\_compiler\.py L382](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/tensorrt_lazy_compiler.py#L382) and [tensorrt\_lazy\_compiler\.py L127](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/tensorrt_lazy_compiler.py#L127) in [`openfold/utils/tensorrt_lazy_compiler.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/tensorrt_lazy_compiler.py) facilitate this optimization\. The [tensorrt\_lazy\_compiler\.py L382](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/tensorrt_lazy_compiler.py#L382) manages the compilation process, converting a PyTorch model into a TensorRT engine\. It allows for dynamic input shapes, meaning the compiled engine can handle inputs of varying sizes without requiring recompilation for each new size\. Precision control is also integrated, allowing users to specify [primitives\.py L52](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/primitives.py#L52) or [tensorrt\_lazy\_compiler\.py L57](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/tensorrt_lazy_compiler.py#L57) precision for inference, which can further boost performance\. The system includes fallback mechanisms to PyTorch execution if TensorRT compilation is not possible or encounters issues\.

 The [config\.py L1010](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/config.py#L1010) component of the OpenFold model is specifically instrumented for TensorRT compilation via functions in [`openfold/utils/tensorrt_utils.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/tensorrt_utils.py)\. This instrumentation manages engine directory creation, defines dynamic shapes for the [config\.py L1010](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/config.py#L1010)'s inputs, and generates input profiles that TensorRT uses for optimization\. This targeted optimization ensures that one of the most computationally intensive parts of the model benefits maximally from TensorRT's acceleration capabilities\.### Advanced Tensor Utilities and Feature Generation

OpenFold utilizes a suite of tensor utility functions to streamline data manipulation and feature generation\. These utilities are general\-purpose, operating on [msa\.py L93](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/model/msa.py#L93) objects, and specialized functions for constructing features from protein data\.

 General\-purpose tensor utilities, primarily found in [`openfold/utils/tensor_utils.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/tensor_utils.py), include:

 - [tensor\_utils\.py L24](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/tensor_utils.py#L24) facilitates conditional type casting of tensors\.
- [tensor\_utils\.py L38](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/tensor_utils.py#L38) and [tensor\_utils\.py L44](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/tensor_utils.py#L44) aid in reshaping tensors by manipulating their trailing dimensions\.
- [tensor\_utils\.py L48](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/tensor_utils.py#L48) calculates the mean of tensor elements while respecting a mask, which is useful for averaging over valid \(unmasked\) data points\.
- [tensor\_utils\.py L53](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/tensor_utils.py#L53) converts sets of points into a distogram, representing the distribution of pairwise distances\.
- [tensor\_utils\.py L83](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/tensor_utils.py#L83) efficiently collects elements from tensors across batch dimensions, which is a common operation in models processing sequences or batches of data\.

 In addition to these general utilities, OpenFold includes functions specifically designed for protein feature generation, primarily within [`openfold/utils/feats.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/feats.py)\. These functions are crucial for transforming raw protein data into numerical features suitable for model input:

 - [feats\.py L35](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/feats.py#L35) computes pseudo\-beta atom coordinates, which are simplified representations of amino acid side chains\. For glycine, the alpha\-carbon is used; otherwise, the beta\-carbon is utilized\.
- [feats\.py L69](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/feats.py#L69) constructs feature vectors from template angles by combining one\-hot encoded amino acid types, torsion angles \(as sine/cosine pairs\), and masks\.
- [feats\.py L110](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/feats.py#L110) generates comprehensive pair features for templates\. This involves integrating distanceograms \(calculated via [feats\.py L93](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/feats.py#L93)\), 2D template masks, one\-hot encoded amino acid types for residue pairs, and relative orientations derived from backbone atoms\.
- [feats\.py L175](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/utils/feats.py#L175) creates features from extra multiple sequence alignment data, typically by concatenating one\-hot encoded MSA entries, deletion flags, and deletion values\.

 These functions are integral to preparing data for the model, ensuring that both structural information and sequence\-based features are correctly formatted and accessible for the protein structure prediction task\. For details on how protein coordinates are converted and represented, refer to [Protein Structural and Coordinate Transformations](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#openfold-utility-functions-and-performance-optimization-protein-structural-and-coordinate-transformations)\. The underlying 3D geometric operations are supported by [Advanced 3D Geometric Data Structures and Operations](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#openfold-utility-functions-and-performance-optimization-advanced-3d-geometric-data-structures-and-operations)\.## Running OpenFold Inference

```
# Set environment variables (refer to inference.sh for full setup)
export FASTA_DIR=./fasta_dir
export OUTPUT_DIR=./
export PRECOMPUTED_ALIGNMENT_DIR=./alignments
export MMCIF_DIR=/mmcifs # UPDATE with path to your mmcifs directory

python3 run_pretrained_openfold.py \
  $FASTA_DIR \
  $MMCIF_DIR \
  --output_dir $OUTPUT_DIR \
  --config_preset model_1_ptm \
  --model_device "cuda:0" \
  --data_random_seed 42 \
  --use_precomputed_alignments $PRECOMPUTED_ALIGNMENT_DIR
```

OpenFold provides an execution framework for protein inference, enabling predictions for monomeric proteins using pretrained models and leveraging precomputed alignments\.

 The directory [`examples`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/examples) contains example scripts demonstrating how to run OpenFold inference\. Specifically, the [`examples/monomer`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/examples/monomer) subdirectory focuses on monomeric protein inference\. An example script, [`examples/monomer/inference.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/examples/monomer/inference.sh), illustrates how to initiate a prediction\. This script utilizes [Dockerfile L32](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/Dockerfile#L32) and allows for the specification of a pretrained model architecture, such as [config\.py L6](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/tests/config.py#L6), via the [Inference\.md?plain=1 L118](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/Inference.md?plain=1#L118) flag\. The script also includes parameters for device selection, like [thread\_sequence\.py L124](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/thread_sequence.py#L124), and sets a random seed for data processing to ensure reproducibility\.

 To optimize the inference process, OpenFold supports the use of precomputed alignments\. The [original\_readme\.md?plain=1 L173](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/original_readme.md?plain=1#L173) flag, as demonstrated in [`examples/monomer/inference.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/examples/monomer/inference.sh), allows the model to leverage existing alignment data, thereby bypassing the need to recompute alignments and potentially accelerating the prediction workflow\.### Running Monomeric Protein Inference

```
# Set environment variables (e.g., FASTA_DIR, OUTPUT_DIR)
# ...

python3 run_pretrained_openfold.py ${FASTA_DIR} \
  ${MMCIF_DIR} \
  --output_dir ${OUTPUT_DIR} \
  --config_preset model_1_ptm \
  --model_device "cuda:0" \
  --data_random_seed 42 \
  --use_precomputed_alignments ${PRECOMPUTED_ALIGNMENT_DIR}
```

Monomeric protein inference in OpenFold is initiated through example scripts that provide command\-line arguments and configuration settings\. The primary script for this purpose is found in the [`examples/monomer`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/examples/monomer) directory\. This script configures the OpenFold model to run inference on single\-chain proteins\. It leverages a specific pretrained model architecture, often denoted by a configuration preset like [config\.py L6](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/tests/config.py#L6), which includes defined parameters for the model\. The execution environment is typically set to a CUDA\-enabled GPU\. To ensure reproducibility of results, a random seed is specified for data processing operations\. Additionally, the inference process can be optimized by using precomputed alignments, which bypass the need for alignment computation and thus accelerate the workflow\. For more details on specifying and using these pretrained models, refer to [Utilizing Pretrained Models for Inference](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#running-openfold-inference-utilizing-pretrained-models-for-inference)\. Further information on integrating precomputed alignments can be found in [Supporting Precomputed Alignments](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#running-openfold-inference-supporting-precomputed-alignments)\.### Utilizing Pretrained Models for Inference

```
# ... other environment variables and script setup
export FASTA_DIR=./fasta_dir
export OUTPUT_DIR=./
export PRECOMPUTED_ALIGNMENT_DIR=./alignments
export MMCIF_DIR=/mmcifs    # UPDATE with path to your mmcifs directory 

python3 run_pretrained_openfold.py $FASTA_DIR \
  $MMCIF_DIR \
  --output_dir $OUTPUT_DIR \
  --config_preset model_1_ptm \
  --model_device "cuda:0" \
  --data_random_seed 42 \
  --use_precomputed_alignments $PRECOMPUTED_ALIGNMENT_DIR
```

OpenFold enables the use of pretrained models for protein structure prediction during inference\. This functionality is configured using the [Inference\.md?plain=1 L118](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/Inference.md?plain=1#L118) flag when executing inference scripts\. For instance, the example inference script located at [`examples/monomer/inference.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/examples/monomer/inference.sh) specifies [config\.py L6](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/tests/config.py#L6) as the preset, indicating that the model should load a specific pretrained architecture and its corresponding parameters\. Different presets correspond to various model configurations trained on different datasets or with varying architectural nuances\. Selecting the appropriate preset allows users to leverage the pre\-trained weights and architectural designs optimized for particular prediction tasks without needing to retrain the model\. This mechanism is central to applying OpenFold effectively for diverse protein structure prediction challenges\.### Supporting Precomputed Alignments

```
# Set environment variables (e.g., CONDA_PREFIX, LIBRARY_PATH)
# ...

export FASTA_DIR=./fasta_dir
export OUTPUT_DIR=./
export PRECOMPUTED_ALIGNMENT_DIR=./alignments
export MMCIF_DIR=/mmcifs    # UPDATE with path to your mmcifs directory 

python3 run_pretrained_openfold.py $FASTA_DIR \
  $MMCIF_DIR \
  --output_dir $OUTPUT_DIR \
  --config_preset model_1_ptm \
  --model_device "cuda:0" \
  --data_random_seed 42 \
  --use_precomputed_alignments $PRECOMPUTED_ALIGNMENT_DIR # Use precomputed alignments from this directory
```

OpenFold supports the integration of precomputed alignments into its inference pipeline, which can accelerate the prediction process by bypassing the computationally intensive alignment generation step\. This functionality is primarily exposed through the example inference script [`examples/monomer/inference.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/examples/monomer/inference.sh)\. The script utilizes the [original\_readme\.md?plain=1 L173](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/original_readme.md?plain=1#L173) flag when executing [Dockerfile L32](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/Dockerfile#L32)\. When this flag is enabled, the model leverages existing alignment data from a specified directory \([inference\.sh L16](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/examples/monomer/inference.sh#L16)\) instead of generating new alignments on the fly\. This is particularly useful for scenarios where multiple predictions are performed on the same protein sequences, allowing for reusability of alignments and faster inference times\. For a general overview of running inference, see [Running OpenFold Inference](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#running-openfold-inference)\.## Experimentation and Model Evaluation

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [config\.py L608](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/config.py#L608) directory, specifically [`experiments`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments), within OpenFold provides a framework for evaluating the performance of protein structure prediction models\. This framework facilitates scoring protein decoys, which are alternative structural predictions for a given protein, and comparing them against known native structures\. The process involves using OpenFold to generate predictions, often with the decoys themselves serving as structural templates, and then quantifying the structural similarity between the predictions, decoys, and native structures\.

 The core of this evaluation framework is in [`experiments/test_templates_openfold.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py)\. This script manages the workflow from preparing input data to analyzing and storing results\. It processes protein sequences and associated decoy structures, then configures and runs an OpenFold model to produce new structural predictions\. A key feature is its ability to use existing PDB structures \(often the decoys themselves\) as templates during the OpenFold prediction process, which can influence the generated structures\.

 After OpenFold generates predictions, the framework calculates various structural similarity metrics\. This includes the Root Mean Square Deviation \(RMSD\) and TM\-score\. RMSD is computed using the Kabsch algorithm for optimal superposition, while TM\-score, which is less sensitive to local errors, is typically calculated by executing an external program\. The results, including predicted PDBs and computed metrics, are systematically saved, and mechanisms are in place to resume evaluations if interrupted\. This ensures persistence and traceability of experimental outcomes\.### Decoy Scoring and Template Preparation

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The process of evaluating protein structure prediction models in OpenFold involves scoring protein decoys and comparing them against native structures\. This begins with preparing candidate decoy structures for use as templates by the OpenFold model\. The [test\_templates\_openfold\.py L217](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py#L217) function in [`experiments/test_templates_openfold.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py) is central to this process, converting a [protein\.py L45](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/np/protein.py#L45) object representing the decoy into features that OpenFold can incorporate into its prediction pipeline\.

 A key aspect of this preparation involves generating template features from the decoy\. OpenFold utilizes these features to inform its structural predictions\. The [test\_templates\_openfold\.py L155](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py#L155) function, detailed in [Model Configuration and Feature Generation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#experimentation-and-model-evaluation-model-configuration-and-feature-generation), combines sequence, MSA, and template information into a comprehensive feature dictionary\. This template generation accounts for potential sequence mismatches between the target protein and the decoy\.

 To manage the level of detail incorporated from decoys, OpenFold provides options for side\-chain masking\. The [test\_templates\_openfold\.py L40](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py#L40) option allows the model to ignore side\-chain atomic coordinates during template processing, focusing only on the backbone\. Alternatively, [test\_templates\_openfold\.py L41](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py#L41) can be used, which specifically adds a C\-beta atom for glycine residues if it is missing, helping to standardize the input for the model\. These masking strategies enable control over the amount of structural information derived from the decoy that is passed to OpenFold, which can be beneficial for specific evaluation scenarios\.### Structural Similarity Metrics and Result Management

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Structural similarity metrics are computed to quantitatively assess the accuracy of predicted protein structures against native structures and input decoys\. The Root Mean Square Deviation \(RMSD\) is calculated using the Kabsch algorithm for optimal superposition, provided by the [test\_templates\_openfold\.py L89](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py#L89) function within [`experiments/test_templates_openfold.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py)\. The TM\-score, another measure of structural similarity, is computed by executing an external TM\-score program\. The [test\_templates\_openfold\.py L303](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py#L303) function in [`experiments/test_templates_openfold.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py) manages this execution and parses the output, including validation of sequence length and common residues\.

 Results are managed to ensure persistence and reproducibility of evaluations\. The [test\_templates\_openfold\.py L332](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py#L332) function in [`experiments/test_templates_openfold.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py) computes additional metrics, saves predicted PDB files, and appends all evaluation data to CSV files\. The system also tracks [test\_templates\_openfold\.py L382](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py#L382) and [test\_templates\_openfold\.py L390](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py#L390) to enable the resumption of interrupted runs, preventing redundant computations\. Metadata for each protein decoy is organized using a [residue\_constants\.py L430](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/np/residue_constants.py#L430) called [test\_templates\_openfold\.py L326](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py#L326)\.### Model Configuration and Feature Generation

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

OpenFold utilizes a structured approach for configuring models and preparing input features for protein structure prediction, particularly during evaluation\. The process involves selecting specific model configurations, managing iterative refinement steps, and generating comprehensive feature dictionaries from various biological inputs\.

 Model configuration is handled by functions such as [test\_templates\_openfold\.py L106](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py#L106) within the evaluation script, allowing for the specification of a [test\_templates\_openfold\.py L434](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py#L434) and the number of [relax\.py L95](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/np/relax/relax.py#L95)—iterations where the model refines its prediction by feeding previous outputs back into itself\. This iterative process is a core component of AlphaFold's architecture\. Further details on this mechanism can be found in [Input Embedding and Recycling Mechanisms](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#alphafold2-model-architecture-implementation-input-embedding-and-recycling-mechanisms)\.

 The generation of features, which serve as the input to the OpenFold model, involves several steps\. ESM1b embeddings are loaded using [test\_templates\_openfold\.py L137](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py#L137) from a specified directory, providing crucial sequence\-level information\. Template features, if available, are prepared using functions like [test\_templates\_openfold\.py L217](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py#L217) from [`experiments/test_templates_openfold.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py)\. This includes options to mask sidechains or to extend glycines with C\-beta atoms\. When no structural templates are used, [test\_templates\_openfold\.py L123](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py#L123) provides an empty set of features\. All these components—sequence features, MSA features, optional template features, and ESM embeddings—are then combined and processed by [test\_templates\_openfold\.py L155](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/experiments/test_templates_openfold.py#L155) using a [thread\_sequence\.py L47](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/thread_sequence.py#L47) to create a unified feature dictionary suitable for the OpenFold model\. This comprehensive feature generation process is vital for providing the model with all necessary information to make accurate predictions\. For a broader understanding of how external bioinformatics tools contribute to this feature generation, refer to [External Tool Integration and Data Pipelines](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#protein-structure-prediction-core-external-tool-integration-and-data-pipelines)\.## OpenFold Scripts and Database Management

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The OpenFold repository includes a suite of scripts designed to manage various aspects of protein structure prediction, from environment setup to data preparation and model optimization\. These scripts are centralized in the [`scripts`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts) directory and its subdirectories, providing tools for both local execution and deployment on cluster environments like SLURM\.

 A core set of scripts facilitates environment management and the installation of third\-party dependencies\. This includes activating and deactivating the Conda environment using [`scripts/activate_conda_env.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/activate_conda_env.sh) and [`scripts/deactivate_conda_env.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/deactivate_conda_env.sh), respectively\. The setup process for external bioinformatics tools like HH\-suite is managed by [`scripts/install_hh_suite.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/install_hh_suite.sh), which handles cloning, building, and installing the software\. Additional scripts, such as [`scripts/install_third_party_dependencies.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/install_third_party_dependencies.sh), handle configuration of environment variables and installation of other necessary components\.

 For protein data acquisition, OpenFold provides extensive scripting for downloading and preparing various biological databases\. This includes [`scripts/download_alphafold_dbs.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_alphafold_dbs.sh), which orchestrates the download of multiple AlphaFold databases like BFD, MGnify, PDB70, and Uniref, with options for full or reduced datasets\. Individual scripts like [`scripts/download_bfd.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_bfd.sh), [`scripts/download_mgnify.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_mgnify.sh), and [`scripts/download_pdb_mmcif.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_pdb_mmcif.sh) handle specific databases, managing their download, decompression, and organization\. OpenFold model parameters, including those for SoloSeq models, can be downloaded from various sources such as Google Cloud Storage, AWS S3, Google Drive, and Hugging Face, using scripts like [`scripts/download_alphafold_params.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_alphafold_params.sh), [`scripts/download_openfold_params.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_openfold_params.sh), and [`scripts/download_openfold_params_huggingface.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_openfold_params_huggingface.sh)\.

 Generating sequence alignments is another crucial aspect covered by these scripts\. The [`scripts/precompute_alignments.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/precompute_alignments.py) script orchestrates the use of external tools like Jackhmmer, HHblits, and HMMsearch to create protein sequence alignments\. For large\-scale alignment generation, especially on SLURM clusters, the [precompute\_alignments\_mmseqs\.py L67](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/precompute_alignments_mmseqs.py#L67) script leverages [colabfold\_search\.sh L4](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/colabfold_search.sh#L4) to perform protein sequence searching and MSA generation against databases such as Uniref and environmental databases\. Related utilities like [`scripts/alignment_data_to_fasta.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/alignment_data_to_fasta.py) convert alignment data into FASTA format\.

 The [`scripts/alignment_db_scripts`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/alignment_db_scripts) directory contains specialized tools for managing alignment databases\. Scripts like [`scripts/alignment_db_scripts/create_alignment_db.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/create_alignment_db.py) and [`scripts/alignment_db_scripts/create_alignment_db_sharded.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/create_alignment_db_sharded.py) consolidate precomputed alignment files into optimized binary databases, while [`scripts/alignment_db_scripts/unify_alignment_db_indices.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/unify_alignment_db_indices.py) combines multiple indices into a single "super index" for efficient lookup\. The script [`scripts/alignment_db_scripts/add_non_unique_to_alignment_db.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/add_non_unique_to_alignment_db.py) extends these indices to include non\-unique protein chains by mapping identical sequences to existing alignment entries\. For intensive alignment tasks, the [`scripts/slurm_scripts/run_uniclust30_search.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/slurm_scripts/run_uniclust30_search.sh) script is designed to generate Uniclust30 all\-against\-all alignments on SLURM clusters, managing database transfer, parallel [hhblits\.py L30](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/hhblits.py#L30) execution, and result compression\.

 Further preprocessing involves generating feature dictionaries and data caches for efficient model training and inference\. Scripts such as [`scripts/generate_alphafold_feature_dict.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/generate_alphafold_feature_dict.py) create AlphaFold feature dictionaries from FASTA inputs, supporting both monomer and multimer predictions\. Similarly, [`scripts/generate_chain_data_cache.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/generate_chain_data_cache.py) and [`scripts/generate_mmcif_cache.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/generate_mmcif_cache.py) generate JSON caches of protein chain data and mmCIF metadata, respectively\.

 OpenFold also provides utilities for performance optimization and model checkpoint management\. The [`scripts/build_deepspeed_config.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/build_deepspeed_config.py) script generates DeepSpeed configuration JSONs, allowing users to customize settings for optimizers, LR schedulers, precision training \(e\.g\., [build\_deepspeed\_config\.py L271](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/build_deepspeed_config.py#L271), [build\_deepspeed\_config\.py L275](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/build_deepspeed_config.py#L275), [build\_deepspeed\_config\.py L266](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/build_deepspeed_config.py#L266)\), activation checkpointing, and ZeRO optimization\. This enables efficient distributed training\. Checkpoint conversion scripts, including [`scripts/convert_of_weights_to_jax.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/convert_of_weights_to_jax.py) and [`scripts/convert_v1_to_v2_weights.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/convert_v1_to_v2_weights.py), handle transformations between OpenFold's PyTorch [thread\_sequence\.py L141](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/thread_sequence.py#L141) format and AlphaFold's JAX [train\_openfold\.py L584](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/train_openfold.py#L584) format, as well as updates for deprecated OpenFold checkpoint versions\.### Environment Setup and Third\-Party Dependencies

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

OpenFold provides scripts to manage its Conda environment and integrate essential third\-party bioinformatics tools and dependencies\. The environment setup is facilitated by [`scripts/activate_conda_env.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/activate_conda_env.sh), which activates a specified Conda environment, and [`scripts/deactivate_conda_env.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/deactivate_conda_env.sh) for deactivation\. For installing core dependencies, [`scripts/install_third_party_dependencies.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/install_third_party_dependencies.sh) downloads necessary stereochemical properties, prepares test data, installs OpenFold, clones NVIDIA's CUTLASS library, and configures crucial environment variables\. Additionally, [`scripts/install_hh_suite.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/install_hh_suite.sh) handles the installation of [install\_hh\_suite\.sh L3](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/install_hh_suite.sh#L3), a collection of tools for remote homology detection and sequence alignment, building it from source and establishing system\-wide symlinks\. These scripts collectively ensure that the OpenFold environment is correctly configured with all external prerequisites for its protein structure prediction tasks\.### AlphaFold and OpenFold Model Parameter Downloads

| Script Name | Model Type | Parameters Downloaded | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| download\_alphafold\_params\.sh | AlphaFold | AlphaFold Parameters | Google Cloud Storage |
| download\_openfold\_params\.sh | OpenFold | OpenFold Parameters | AWS S3 |
| download\_openfold\_params\_gdrive\.sh | OpenFold | OpenFold Parameters | Google Drive |
| download\_openfold\_params\_huggingface\.sh | OpenFold | OpenFold Parameters | Hugging Face |
| download\_openfold\_soloseq\_params\.sh | OpenFold SoloSeq | OpenFold SoloSeq Parameters | AWS S3 |
| download\_soloseq\_embeddings\.sh | OpenFold SoloSeq | ESM\-1b Embeddings | AWS S3 |

Pre\-trained model parameters are essential for leveraging OpenFold's protein structure prediction capabilities without extensive retraining\. OpenFold provides scripts to download these parameters from various sources for both AlphaFold and OpenFold models\.

 For AlphaFold model parameters, the [Inference\.md?plain=1 L34](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/Inference.md?plain=1#L34) script facilitates downloading the necessary [train\_openfold\.py L584](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/train_openfold.py#L584) files from Google Cloud Storage\. Similarly, OpenFold's own pre\-trained parameters can be acquired via [Inference\.md?plain=1 L40](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/Inference.md?plain=1#L40) from an AWS S3 bucket\. Alternative download methods are also available; [Installation\.md?plain=1 L66](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/Installation.md?plain=1#L66) supports downloading OpenFold parameters from Google Drive, while [Installation\.md?plain=1 L65](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/Installation.md?plain=1#L65) utilizes [Installation\.md?plain=1 L15](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/Installation.md?plain=1#L15) to retrieve them from a Hugging Face repository\. For specialized single\-sequence models, the [Installation\.md?plain=1 L38](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/Installation.md?plain=1#L38) script is available to fetch parameters for the OpenFold SoloSeq model from AWS S3, and [download\_soloseq\_embeddings\.sh L19](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_soloseq_embeddings.sh#L19) downloads corresponding ESM\-1b embeddings\.

 The management of these downloaded parameters and other biological databases is further detailed in [Biological Database Acquisition and Preparation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#openfold-scripts-and-database-management-biological-database-acquisition-and-preparation)\. Once downloaded, these parameters can be converted or managed using utilities described in [Checkpoint Conversion Utilities](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#openfold-scripts-and-database-management-checkpoint-conversion-utilities)\.### Biological Database Acquisition and Preparation

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

OpenFold relies on a comprehensive set of biological databases to perform protein structure prediction\. These databases provide essential sequence and structural information that the model uses for tasks such as MSA generation and template identification\. The system includes a suite of scripts designed to automate the acquisition, preparation, and management of these large datasets\. These scripts handle everything from downloading raw data to organizing it into formats suitable for OpenFold's processing pipelines\.

 Central to this data acquisition process is the [Inference\.md?plain=1 L18](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/Inference.md?plain=1#L18) script, which orchestrates the download of various databases required by AlphaFold, including BFD, MGnify, PDB70, PDB mmCIF, Uniref, UniProt, and PDB SeqRes\. This script acts as a master control, invoking specialized sub\-scripts for each database\. For instance, the script utilizes [download\_bfd\.sh L19](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_bfd.sh#L19) or [download\_small\_bfd\.sh L19](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_small_bfd.sh#L19) to acquire the BFD database, depending on whether a full or reduced dataset is desired\. Similarly, [download\_mgnify\.sh L19](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_mgnify.sh#L19) fetches the MGnify protein sequence database, and [download\_pdb70\.sh L19](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_pdb70.sh#L19) is responsible for the PDB70 dataset\.

 The acquisition of structural data is managed by [download\_pdb\_mmcif\.sh L19](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_pdb_mmcif.sh#L19), which downloads and flattens the PDB mmCIF database, making CIF files readily accessible\. Complementing this, [original\_readme\.md?plain=1 L297](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/original_readme.md?plain=1#L297) specifically targets the PDB SeqRes database, filtering it to retain only protein sequences\. Specialized scripts are also available for downloading other large sequence databases, such as [download\_uniclust30\.sh L19](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_uniclust30.sh#L19) for Uniclust30, [download\_uniprot\.sh L20](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_uniprot.sh#L20) for UniProt, [original\_readme\.md?plain=1 L304](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/original_readme.md?plain=1#L304) for Uniref30, and [download\_uniref90\.sh L19](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_uniref90.sh#L19) for Uniref90\. These scripts often leverage tools like [download\_bfd\.sh L27](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_bfd.sh#L27) for efficient parallel downloading and [download\_bfd\.sh L35](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_bfd.sh#L35) or [download\_mgnify\.sh L41](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_mgnify.sh#L41) for decompression\.

 Beyond these foundational databases, OpenFold also incorporates data from community\-driven projects\. For example, [original\_readme\.md?plain=1 L95](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/original_readme.md?plain=1#L95) manages the download of MMSeqs2\-related databases, including those from ColabFold\. This script, in turn, calls [download\_mmseqs\_dbs\.sh L46](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_mmseqs_dbs.sh#L46) to obtain the ColabFold environmental database\. For researchers focusing on specific benchmarks, [original\_readme\.md?plain=1 L433](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/original_readme.md?plain=1#L433) facilitates the download of CAMEO protein data, including CIF files and corresponding FASTA sequences, with optional filtering by sequence length\. The system also supports scenario\-specific downloads, such as [download\_roda\_pdbs\.sh L20](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/download_roda_pdbs.sh#L20) which downloads protein CIF files from RCSB matching RODA alignments\.

 In addition to downloading, the system includes utilities for preparing these datasets\. For instance, [original\_readme\.md?plain=1 L405](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/original_readme.md?plain=1#L405) converts directories containing protein structure files \([Inference\.md?plain=1 L141](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/Inference.md?plain=1#L141), [data\_dir\_to\_fasta\.py L35](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/data_dir_to_fasta.py#L35), or [unpack\_proteinnet\.py L8](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/unpack_proteinnet.py#L8)\) into a single FASTA file\. [OpenFold\_Training\_Setup\.md?plain=1 L97](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/OpenFold_Training_Setup.md?plain=1#L97) clusters sequences from FASTA files using [index\.md?plain=1 L51](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/index.md?plain=1#L51), while [OpenFold\_Training\_Setup\.md?plain=1 L64](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/OpenFold_Training_Setup.md?plain=1#L64) expands alignment databases by creating symbolic links for duplicate PDB chains\. These preparation steps ensure that the diverse array of biological data is uniformly formatted and optimized for use in downstream processes, including the generation of features for the core model\.### Protein Alignment Generation and Processing

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

OpenFold utilizes several scripts to generate protein sequence alignments, which are crucial for subsequent protein structure prediction\. These alignments are generated using external bioinformatics tools and then processed into a format usable by the OpenFold model\.

 The primary script for orchestrating alignment precomputation is [original\_readme\.md?plain=1 L372](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/original_readme.md?plain=1#L372) in [`scripts`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts)\. This script leverages various tools, including JackHMMER, HHblits, HMMsearch, and HHSearch, to perform sequence searches and generate alignments\. It handles input parsing from diverse formats, such as mmCIF, FASTA, and ProteinNet [unpack\_proteinnet\.py L8](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/unpack_proteinnet.py#L8) files, and supports multithreading for efficient execution\. The [precompute\_alignments\.py L23](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/precompute_alignments.py#L23) function within this script manages sequence grouping and alignment, while [precompute\_alignments\.py L66](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/precompute_alignments.py#L66) is responsible for processing different input formats\.

 For scenarios requiring MMseqs2, OpenFold uses [precompute\_alignments\_mmseqs\.py L67](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/precompute_alignments_mmseqs.py#L67) in [`scripts`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts)\. This shell script executes a complex [colabfold\_search\.sh L4](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/colabfold_search.sh#L4) workflow to generate multiple sequence alignments \(MSAs\) and identify templates\. It performs searches against databases like Uniref and environmental databases \(e\.g\., BFD\) to produce [data\_modules\.py L56](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_modules.py#L56) files, which contain MSAs\. Additionally, it can identify PDB templates, outputting them in [colabfold\_search\.sh L57](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/colabfold_search.sh#L57) format\. The workflow involves multiple [colabfold\_search\.sh L4](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/colabfold_search.sh#L4) commands, including [train\_openfold\.py L481](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/train_openfold.py#L481), [colabfold\_search\.sh L45](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/colabfold_search.sh#L45), [kalign\.py L50](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/tools/kalign.py#L50), [colabfold\_search\.sh L49](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/colabfold_search.sh#L49), and [colabfold\_search\.sh L50](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/colabfold_search.sh#L50), to refine the search results and generate the final MSAs\.

 After initial alignment generation, a separate Python script, [original\_readme\.md?plain=1 L393](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/original_readme.md?plain=1#L393) in [`scripts`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts), processes these outputs further\. It uses [index\.md?plain=1 L51](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/index.md?plain=1#L51) \(via [precompute\_alignments\_mmseqs\.py L67](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/precompute_alignments_mmseqs.py#L67)\) and [original\_readme\.md?plain=1 L390](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/original_readme.md?plain=1#L390) to refine alignments, splitting [data\_modules\.py L56](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/data/data_modules.py#L56) files and generating [Aux\_seq\_files\.md?plain=1 L29](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/Aux_seq_files.md?plain=1#L29) files, which are essential for template identification\.

 The outputs from these alignment generation processes are then used to build feature dictionaries and caches, which prepare the data for the OpenFold model [Feature and Chain Data Cache Generation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#openfold-scripts-and-database-management-feature-and-chain-data-cache-generation)\. These processed alignments are stored in specialized alignment databases, which are managed by scripts designed for creating, sharding, and unifying indices to optimize storage and retrieval [Alignment Database Creation and Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#openfold-scripts-and-database-management-alignment-database-creation-and-management)\.### Alignment Database Creation and Management

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

OpenFold includes a set of scripts dedicated to managing and optimizing protein alignment databases, which are crucial for efficient data retrieval during model training and inference\. These scripts, located in the [`scripts/alignment_db_scripts`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/alignment_db_scripts) directory, address challenges related to storing and accessing large volumes of precomputed alignments\.

 The process of creating an alignment database involves consolidating numerous individual alignment files into a more efficient format\. The script [`scripts/alignment_db_scripts/create_alignment_db.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/create_alignment_db.py) handles this by combining precomputed alignment files from a directory structure into a single binary [create\_alignment\_db\.py L7](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/create_alignment_db.py#L7) file, accompanied by a JSON [residue\_constants\.py L1148](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/np/residue_constants.py#L1148) file that maps protein chain identifiers to their data within the [create\_alignment\_db\.py L7](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/create_alignment_db.py#L7) file\. This approach centralizes alignment data, reducing file system overhead and improving lookup times\.

 For very large datasets, a sharded database approach can further enhance performance and manageability\. The [`scripts/alignment_db_scripts/create_alignment_db_sharded.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/create_alignment_db_sharded.py) script generates a sharded alignment database, distributing alignment data across multiple [create\_alignment\_db\.py L7](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/create_alignment_db.py#L7) files\. It creates a [unify\_alignment\_db\_indices\.py L10](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/unify_alignment_db_indices.py#L10) \(a JSON dictionary\) that tracks which shard contains the data for a given chain, leveraging parallel processing to accelerate shard creation\. This sharding strategy is particularly beneficial for distributed training environments\.

 To facilitate querying across multiple shards or combining indices from different database creation runs, the [`scripts/alignment_db_scripts/unify_alignment_db_indices.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/unify_alignment_db_indices.py) script aggregates several individual [residue\_constants\.py L1148](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/openfold/np/residue_constants.py#L1148) files into a single [original\_readme\.md?plain=1 L476](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/docs/source/original_readme.md?plain=1#L476) JSON file\. This unified index provides a comprehensive mapping of sequence identifiers to their respective database names and file locations, streamlining data access\.

 Finally, the [`scripts/alignment_db_scripts/add_non_unique_to_alignment_db.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/add_non_unique_to_alignment_db.py) script addresses the challenge of non\-unique protein chains—cases where multiple PDB entries might have identical or near\-identical sequences but distinct identifiers\. This script extends an existing [unify\_alignment\_db\_indices\.py L10](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/unify_alignment_db_indices.py#L10) to include these non\-unique chains, mapping them to pre\-existing alignment entries for chains with the same sequence\. This prevents redundant storage of identical alignments and ensures that all relevant chains can be correctly linked to their alignment data\.

 Together, these scripts provide a robust framework for managing protein alignment databases, enabling efficient storage, retrieval, and scaling for diverse protein structure prediction tasks within OpenFold\. Other scripts for general database acquisition are discussed in [Biological Database Acquisition and Preparation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#openfold-scripts-and-database-management-biological-database-acquisition-and-preparation), and alignment generation in [Protein Alignment Generation and Processing](https://codewiki.google/github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold#openfold-scripts-and-database-management-protein-alignment-generation-and-processing)\.### Feature and Chain Data Cache Generation

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Scripts located within the [`scripts`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/blob/be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d/scripts) directory are responsible for generating crucial caches that preprocess data for protein structure prediction, serving as intermediaries between raw biological databases and the OpenFold model\. These preprocessing steps are essential for both training and inference\.

 One key utility is the generation of AlphaFold feature dictionaries, which are structured representations of input data ready for model consumption\.
